problem_statement: The Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store only supports 32-bit identifiers: its public API takes a uint32_t id, and its on-flash allocation table entry (ATE) reserves 32 bits for the id. Applications that need an identifier namespace larger than 32 bits cannot use ZMS. Add optional support for 64-bit identifiers: a zms_id_t type whose width is selected at build time by a Kconfig option, a corresponding ATE format that reserves 64 bits for the id, and the matching write/read/delete/history behaviour so that entries with 64-bit ids can be stored, looked up, and read back correctly (including distinguishing ids that share the same low 32 bits but differ in the high 32 bits).

verification.reason: The statement captures the feature but omits exact names and several observable behaviors that the hidden tests require, all of which can be added without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests require the Kconfig option CONFIG_ZMS_ID_64BIT, but the problem statement only says a Kconfig option selects the ID width without giving its name.
The hidden tests use the macros ZMS_ATE_FORMAT_MASK and ZMS_DEFAULT_ATE_FORMAT to construct/validate empty ATE metadata, but the statement does not mention these names.
The test configuration enables CONFIG_ZMS_LOOKUP_CACHE and relies on the lookup cache working correctly with 64-bit IDs, which is not stated in the problem.
The 64-bit ATE format leaves only 4 bytes for small data, so an 8-byte value must be stored outside the ATE; this observable consequence is not stated.
The special identifier ZMS_HEAD_ID must be the all-ones value of the selected zms_id_t width, but the statement does not state this.

problem_statement_fixed: The Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store only supports 32-bit identifiers: its public API takes a uint32_t id, and its on-flash allocation table entry (ATE) reserves 32 bits for the id. Applications that need an identifier namespace larger than 32 bits cannot use ZMS. Add optional support for 64-bit identifiers: a zms_id_t type whose width is selected at build time by the Kconfig option CONFIG_ZMS_ID_64BIT, a corresponding ATE format that reserves 64 bits for the id, and the matching write/read/delete/history behaviour so that entries with 64-bit ids can be stored, looked up, and read back correctly (including distinguishing ids that share the same low 32 bits but differ in the high 32 bits). The public ZMS API functions that take an id must use zms_id_t. The selected ATE format must be indicated in the metadata field of the empty ATE using the macro ZMS_ATE_FORMAT_MASK, with the selected format given by ZMS_DEFAULT_ATE_FORMAT; ZMS_DEFAULT_ATE_FORMAT must select the 32-bit format when CONFIG_ZMS_ID_64BIT is disabled and the 64-bit format when it is enabled. The capacity for data stored inline in an ATE must follow the selected ATE layout (8 bytes for the 32-bit format, 4 bytes for the 64-bit format), and all identifier-dependent code, including the optional lookup cache, must operate on zms_id_t.
